newsitem.title: USA: Two U.S. senators vow to protect ethanol tax break.
newsitem.headline: Two U.S. senators vow to protect ethanol tax break.

text.p: Two U.S. farm state senators vowed on Wednesday to fight any effort to eliminate a tax break for ethanol, which is distilled from corn.

Senate Minority Leader Tom Daschle, D-S.D., and Sen. Tom Harkin, D-Iowa, cited comments last week by House Ways and Means Committee chairman Bill Archer, R-Texas, who called the ethanol tax credit "an anachronism".
"When Bill Archer and the Big Oil crowd tried to kill ethanol in the past, common sense won out and we stopped them," Harkin said in a statement.
"If he wants to grab that tiger by the tail again, it's up to him, but he's in for a real battle," Harkin added.
Oil refiners have long fought the 5.4 cents tax credit which which ethanol blenders receive on the 18.3 cents oer gallon federal gasoline tax.
Harkin said the ethanol subsidy was needed to promote the use of "home-grown" energy sources which would reducing the need for imported oil, and promote a cleaner environment.
